translation.title: Abundance (al-Kawthar)
notes: English translation added as 'text_en' (segments, footnotes), 'lemma_en' (lemma headings) and '*_en' metadata fields; all original Arabic fields are unchanged. Segment boundaries follow the printed pages, so some sentences are split across segments.

x: Commentary on the Surah "al-Kawthar". In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted, whose names are sanctified:
h
Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar (1) So pray to your Lord and sacrifice (2) Indeed, your hater is the one cut off (3)
. He, mighty be His mention, says: We have given you, Muhammad, al-Kawthar.
The people of interpretation differed over the meaning of al-Kawthar.
Some of them said: It is a river in Paradise that God gave to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, that he said:
m: Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, with banks of gold and silver, flowing over pearls and rubies; its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from 'Ata', from Muharib ibn Dithar al-Bahili, from Ibn 'Umar,
m: Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar
. He said: A river in Paradise, with banks of gold, its course over pearls and rubies, its water whiter than snow and sweeter than honey, and its soil more fragrant than the scent of musk

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Umar ibn 'Ubayd related to us, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:
m: Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, with banks of gold and silver, flowing over rubies and pearls; its water is whiter than snow and sweeter than honey

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi related to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shimr ibn 'Atiyyah, from Shaqiq,
m: or Masruq, who said: I said to 'A'ishah: Mother of the Believers, [tell me about al-Kawthar]

. She said: A river in the bellies (butnan) of Paradise. I said: What are the bellies of Paradise? She said: The middle of Paradise; its banks are palaces of pearl and ruby, its soil is musk, and its gravel is pearl and ruby

c: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraij al-Razi related to us, saying: Abu al-Nadr and Shababah related to us,
m: both saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from a man, from 'A'ishah, who said: Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise; no one puts his two fingers in his ears but he hears the murmur of that river

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Abu Ja'far; and Ibn Abi Suraij related to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Anas, who said:
m: Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise
. He said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'A'ishah, who said: Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, of hollow pearl
: Waki' related to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'A'ishah: Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, on which there are vessels as many as the stars of the sky
. He said: Waki' related to us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'A'ishah, who said: Whoever wants to hear the murmur of al-Kawthar, let him put his two fingers in his ears

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'A'ishah, who said:
m: A river in Paradise whose two shores are hollow pearl. He said: Mihran related to us, from Abu Mu'adh 'Isa ibn Yazid, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'A'ishah, who said: Al-Kawthar is a river in the bellies of Paradise, the middle of Paradise; in it is a river whose two shores are hollow pearl, and in it are vessels for the people of Paradise as many as the stars of the sky.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar
. He said: A river that God gave to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, in Paradise

c: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraij related to us, saying: Mas'adah related to us, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from Mujahid, who said:
m: Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, its soil fragrant musk and its water wine

c: Ibn Abi Suraij related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: Abu Ja'far informed us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah,
m: Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar
. He said: A river in Paradise (4).

c: Al-Rabi' related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Sharik ibn Abi Namir, who said:
m: I heard Anas ibn Malik relate to us, saying: When the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was taken on the Night Journey, Gabriel went with him in the lowest heaven, and there was a river with a palace of pearl and chrysolite upon it. He went to smell its soil, and it was musk. He said: "Gabriel, what is this river?" He said: It is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has kept in store for you

x: Others said: By al-Kawthar is meant abundant good.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to me, saying: Abu Bishr and 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said
m: of al-Kawthar: It is the abundant good that God gave him. Abu Bishr said: I said to Sa'id ibn Jubayr: People claim that it is a river in Paradise. Sa'id said: The river that is in Paradise is part of the good that God gave him

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, who said:
m: Muharib ibn Dithar said to me: What did Sa'id ibn Jubayr say about al-Kawthar? I said: He said: Ibn 'Abbas said: It is abundant good. He said: By God, he spoke the truth.

c: Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:
Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Bishr, who said:
m: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about al-Kawthar, and he said: It is the abundant good that God gave him. I said to Sa'id: We used to hear that it is a river in Paradise. He said: It is the good that God gave him

c: Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad related to me, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr:
m: Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar

c: Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muhammad related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from 'Umarah ibn Abi Hafsah, from 'Ikrimah, who said:
m: It is prophethood, and the good that God gave him

c: Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Harami ibn 'Umarah related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, saying: 'Umarah informed me, from 'Ikrimah,
m: Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar
. He said: Abundant good, the Qur'an and wisdom.

c: Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Umarah ibn Abi Hafsah related to us, from 'Ikrimah, that he said:
Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar
. He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Hilal, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr:
Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar
. He said: God gave him a great deal of good. I said: A river in Paradise? He said: A river and other things.

c: Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa ibn Maymun, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said:
Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa' related to us,
m: all together from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said:

c: Al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waraqa' related to us, from Mujahid:
Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said:
m: The good of this world and the next

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah,
m: on al-Kawthar, who said: It is abundant good.

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: : abundant good. He said: Waki' related to us, from Badr ibn 'Uthman, who heard 'Ikrimah say about al-Kawthar: It is the good, prophethood and Qur'an that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was given

c: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraij al-Razi related to us, saying: Abu Dawud related to us, from Badr, from 'Ikrimah,
m: Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar
. He said: The good that God gave him: prophethood and Islam.

x: Others said: It is a pool (hawd) that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was given in Paradise.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us,
m: Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar
. He said: A pool in Paradise that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was given

c: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraij related to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, saying:
m: Fitr (1) related to us, saying: I asked 'Ata', while we were circumambulating the House, about His saying:
Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar

. He said: A pool that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was given. The most correct of these views, in my opinion, is the view of those who said: It is the name of the river that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was given in Paradise, which God described as abundant because of the greatness of its worth. I say that this is the most correct of the views on this because of the succession of reports from the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, that it is so.

x: Mention of the reports that came to this effect:

c: Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam al-'Ijli related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, saying:
m: I heard my father relate from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: When the Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was taken up into Paradise, or as he said, a river appeared before him, its banks of hollow ruby, or he said "mujawwab". The angel who was with him struck it with his hand and brought out musk. Muhammad said to the angel who was with him: "What is this?" He said: This is al-Kawthar which God has given you. He said: And the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary was raised for him, and he saw beside it a great sign. Or as he said

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas,
m: that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "While I was walking in Paradise, a river appeared before me, its banks domes of hollow pearl. The angel who was with me
said: Do you know what this is? This is al-Kawthar which God has given you. And he struck his hand to its ground and brought out from its mud musk

c: Ibn 'Awf related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: Shayban related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "When I was taken up to the heaven, I came upon a river whose banks were domes of hollow pearl. I said: What is this, Gabriel? He said: This is al-Kawthar which your Lord has given you. And the angel reached out his hand and brought out its mud as fragrant musk

c: Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Humayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I entered Paradise, and there was a river whose banks were tents of pearl. I struck my hand into what flowed in it, and it was fragrant musk." He said: "I said: What is this, Gabriel? He said: This is al-Kawthar which God has given you

c: Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, saying: Qatadah related to us, from Anas, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said. Then he mentioned something like the report of Yazid, from Sa'id, [that which Bishr related to us]

c: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraij related to us, saying: Abu Ayyub al-'Abbas related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd related to us, saying:
m: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim, the nephew of Ibn Shihab, related to me, from his father, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked about al-Kawthar, and he said: "It is a river that God gave me in Paradise, its soil musk, whiter than milk and sweeter than honey; birds come to it whose necks are like the necks of camels." Abu Bakr said: Messenger of God, those are delightful. He said: "Those who eat them are more delightful than they"

c: Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, saying: [al-Nadr informed us, saying
m: Waqqas al-Laythi informed us, from Kathir, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I entered Paradise when I was taken up, and I was given al-Kawthar. It is a river in Paradise, its two doorposts ('idadatah)

c: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam related to me, saying: My father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth related to us, from al-Layth, from Yazid ibn al-Had, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from Anas,
m: that a man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: Messenger of God, what is al-Kawthar? He said: "A river that God gave me in Paradise; it is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and in it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." 'Umar said: Messenger of God, those are delightful. He said: "Those who eat them are more delightful than they"

c: Yunus related to us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: al-Layth related to me, from Ibn al-Had, from 'Abd al-Wahhab, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Shihab, from Anas,
m: that a man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Then he mentioned the like of it

c: ['Umar ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri related to us, that his brother 'Abd Allah informed him
m: , that Anas ibn Malik, a Companion of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed him that a man asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: What is al-Kawthar? The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "It is a river that God gave me in Paradise; its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and in it are birds whose necks are like the necks of camels." 'Umar said: Those are delightful, Messenger of God. He said: "Those who eat them are more delightful than they"
. 'Umar ibn 'Uthman said: Ibn Abi Uways said:

c: My father also related to me, from the nephew of al-Zuhri, from his father, from Anas, from the Prophet,
m: peace and blessings be upon him, about al-Kawthar, the like of it

c: Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, saying: 'Ata' related to us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, its two banks of gold, its course over rubies and pearls, its soil more fragrant than musk, its water sweeter than honey and whiter than snow

c: Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, saying:
m: Muharib ibn Dithar said to me: What did Sa'id ibn Jubayr say about al-Kawthar? I said: He related to us from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: It is abundant good. He said: By God, he spoke the truth, it is indeed abundant good; but Ibn 'Umar related to us, saying: When
Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar
was revealed, the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise, its two banks of gold, flowing over pearls and rubies"

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik,
m: that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise." The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "I saw a river whose banks were pearl, and I said: What is this, Gabriel? He said: This is al-Kawthar which God has given you"

c: Ibn al-Barqi related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir related to us, saying:
m: ibn 'Uthman informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Usamah ibn Zayd, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, came one day to Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and did not find him, so he asked his wife about him, and she was of Banu al-Najjar. She said: He went out, may my father be your ransom, a moment ago heading toward you, and I think he missed you in one of the lanes of Banu al-Najjar. Will you not come in, Messenger of God? So he went in, and she offered him hays
, and he ate of it. She said: Messenger of God, may it be wholesome and agreeable to you. You came when I was wanting to come to you to congratulate you and wish you well:
b.via: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir

c: Abu 'Umarah informed me that
m: you have been given a river in Paradise called al-Kawthar. He said: "Yes, and its width (meaning its ground) is ruby, coral, chrysolite and pearl"

x: And His saying:
h
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
The people of interpretation differed over the prayer that God commanded His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to pray in this address, and over the meaning of His saying
h
and sacrifice (wa-nhar)
Some of them said: He urged him to keep up the obligatory prayer and to guard it in its times by His saying
h
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
Mention of those who said that:

c: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad al-Tufawi related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad ibn Abi al-Ja'd related to me, from 'Asim al-Jahdari, from 'Uqbah ibn Zuhayr, from 'Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, on His saying:
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: Placing the right hand on the left in prayer.

c: Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from 'Asim al-Jahdari, from 'Uqbah ibn Zabyan, from his father, from 'Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him:
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: Placing the hand on the hand in prayer.

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from 'Asim al-Jahdari,
m: , from his father, from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him:
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice

. He said: Placing his right hand on the middle of his left forearm, then placing them on his chest. He said: Mihran related to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from al-Sha'bi, the same

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from 'Asim al-Jahdari, from 'Uqbah ibn Zuhayr, from 'Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him:
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice

c: Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Awf related to us, from Abu al-Qamus,
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: Placing the hand on the hand in prayer.

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Abu Salih al-Khurasani related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, from 'Asim al-Jahdari, from his father, from 'Uqbah ibn Zabyan,
m: that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said on the saying of God:
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: Placing his right hand on the middle of his left forearm, then placing them on his chest

x: Others said: Rather, by His saying
h
So pray to your Lord
the obligatory prayer is meant, and by His saying
h
and sacrifice
that he raise his hands to the neck (nahr) at the opening of the prayer and entering into it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far:
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
: he raises his hands the first time he says the takbir at the opening

x: Others said: By His saying
h
So pray to your Lord
the obligatory prayer is meant, and by His saying
h
and sacrifice
the slaughter of the sacrificial camels (budn).
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm and Harun ibn al-Mughirah related to us, from 'Anbasah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid:
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: The obligatory prayer and the slaughter of the sacrificial camels

c: Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr,
m: , that they both said on His saying:
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: The morning prayer at Jam', and the slaughter of the sacrificial camels at Mina

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us,
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: The dawn prayer, and slaughter the camels

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: The obligatory prayer, and the sacrifice (nahr) is the offering (nusuk) and the slaughter on the Day of the Sacrifice (al-Adha)

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam,
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant is: pray the 'Id prayer on the Day of the Sacrifice, and sacrifice your offering.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughirah related to us, from 'Anbasah, from Jabir, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:
m: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to sacrifice before praying, so he was commanded to pray and then sacrifice

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from 'Ikrimah:
m: Pray the prayer and sacrifice the offering

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Thabit ibn Abi Safiyyah, from Abu Ja'far:
m: . He said: The prayer. And 'Ikrimah said: The prayer and the sacrifice of the offering.

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi':
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: When you have prayed on the Day of al-Adha, sacrifice (2).

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying:
m: related to us, saying: I asked 'Ata' about His saying:
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: You pray and you sacrifice

c: Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Awf related to us, from al-Hasan:
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: Slaughter. He said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying:

c: Aban ibn Khalid related to us, saying:
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah:
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: The slaughter of the sacrificial camels, and the prayer on the Day of Sacrifice.

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah:
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: The prayer of al-Adha, and the sacrifice is the slaughter of the camels

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid:
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: The slaughter places of the camels at Mina

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from 'Ikrimah:
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: The sacrifice of the offering (4).

c: 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas,
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He says: Slaughter on the Day of the Sacrifice

c: Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: The slaughter of the camels.

x: Others said: This was said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, because there were people who prayed to other than God and sacrificed to other than Him, so he was told: Make your prayer and your sacrifice for God, since whoever disbelieves in God makes it for other than Him.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr related to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi,
m: that he used to say about this verse:
Indeed, We have given you al-Kawthar (1) So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He says: Some people used to pray to other than God and sacrifice to other than God, so when We have given you al-Kawthar, Muhammad, let your prayer and your sacrifice be for none but Me

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and his Companions were besieged and barred from the House, and God commanded him to pray, to slaughter the camels, and to depart, and he did so.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said:
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice

, was on the day of al-Hudaybiyah; Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said: Sacrifice and go back. So the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, stood up and delivered [the sermon of al-Fitr and al-Nahr]
, then prayed two rak'ahs, then went to the sacrificial camels and slaughtered them. That is when He says:
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: pray, and call upon your Lord and ask Him.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak:
m: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice
. He said: Pray to your Lord and ask
. One of the people of Arabic

as: and face the qiblah with your chest (nahr). He mentioned that he heard some Arabs say: "Their houses are nahr to one another", meaning: this one is facing (bi-nahr) that one, i.e. opposite it. And he mentioned that one of Banu Asad recited to him: "Abu Hakam, are you not the paternal uncle of Mujalid, and the chief of the people of al-Abtah, the mutanahir?" meaning: some of them slaughter (yanharu) others. The most correct of these views in my opinion is the view of those who said: the meaning is: make all your prayer purely for your Lord, apart from every other rival and god, and likewise your sacrifice, make it for Him rather than for idols, in gratitude to Him for the honor and the incomparable good that He gave you and singled you out with, in giving you al-Kawthar. I say that this is the most correct of the views on this because God, glorified be His mention, informed His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, of the gift, honor and favor with which He had honored him in al-Kawthar, and then followed that with His saying
So pray to your Lord and sacrifice

. So it is known from that that He singled him out for prayer to Him and sacrifice in gratitude to Him, for the blessing of which He had informed him, in giving him al-Kawthar. So there is no basis for specifying one kind of prayer for that rather than another, or one kind of sacrifice rather than another, since gratitude for blessings is a duty. The meaning of the passage, then, is: We have given you, Muhammad, al-Kawthar, as a favor from Us to you and an honor from Us for you; so devote worship purely to your Lord, and single out for Him your prayer and your offerings, contrary to what is done by those who disbelieve in Him, worship other than Him, and sacrifice to idols.

Indeed, your hater is the one cut off
is the contemptible, the insignificant, the abased

m: Indeed, your hater is the one cut off

m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying:

. He said: The man says: Muhammad is cut off; as you see, he has no offspring. So God said:

m: 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt used to say: No son will remain for the Prophet
, and he is cut off. So God sent down about him these verses:

x: Others said: Rather, a group of Quraysh is meant.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Ikrimah,
m: Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture who believe in Jibt and Taghut and say of those who disbelieve, 'These are better guided in the way than those who believe'
[al-Nisa': (51)]. He said: It was revealed about Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, who came to Mecca, and its people said to him: We are better, or is this sunbur

, cut off from his people? We are the people of the pilgrimage, and we have the slaughter place of the sacrificial camels. He said: You are better. So God sent down about him this verse, and sent down about those who said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, what they said:
Indeed, your hater is the one cut off

c: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Badr ibn 'Uthman, from 'Ikrimah:
m: Indeed, your hater is the one cut off
. He said: When revelation came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, Quraysh said: Muhammad has been cut off from us. So
Indeed, your hater is the one cut off
was revealed. He said: The one who threw "cutting off" at you is the one cut off

c: Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind informed us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:
m: When Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf came to Mecca they went to him and said to him: We are the people of the watering (siqayah) and the custodianship (sidanah) of the Ka'bah, and you are the master of the people of Medina; so are we better or this sunbur cut off from his people, who claims that he is better than us? He said: Rather, you are better than he. He
Indeed, your hater is the one cut off
was revealed to him. He said: And there was revealed to him:
Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture

. The most correct of the views on this in my opinion is to say: God, mighty be His mention, informed that the one who hates the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, is the lesser, the humbled, the one whose line is cut off. That is the description of everyone who hates him among people, even if the verse was revealed about one particular person. End of the commentary on Surat al-Kawthar.

notes.en: Ṣunbūr means “one cut off.” Originally, a ṣunbūr is a palm shoot growing from the trunk rather than from the ground; it is also said to be a solitary palm with a slender base. The meaning is that when he is uprooted, his memory is cut off, as the trace of a ṣunbūr disappears, since he has no descendants. Al-Nihāya, 3/55.
